correctness.rationale: Prime-exponent coordinates identify the pure divisibility structures exactly with products of three finite chains of lengths at least two; permuting factors is an isomorphism. In the three-round chain game, corresponding gaps with r moves left can be kept equal or both of size at least 2^r−1: copy small subgaps and leave both sides large when neither subgap is small. Running this strategy in each coordinate preserves all product equality and order tests, yielding the cap seven. For a selected ordered pair, the four-valued comparisons to a third point, together with the ordered pair's own comparison, determine the entire triple diagram including repeats. Taking sets of extensions twice more is the exact rank-three criterion. Local four-bit supports combine by intersection since the third point's coordinates are independent. A separate full-vertex bitset checker reproduced all 56 case rows and memberships in classification.json, the printed 35-triple table, and all 36 ordered choices of the two other sides for replacing six by seven. That test, combined with cap seven, justifies successive coordinate replacements at any sizes. Capping never increases volume. Comparing all capped class minima establishes the sharp maximum 150 at T25, attained by (5,5,6).
residual_risks: The computation verifies the finite classification and cutoff comparisons only; the infinite reduction is the separate game proof. The bound is within the exactly-three-prime family.

The exact table decides low-rank definability across all exponent triples, including cross-size collapses not predicted by the coordinate strategy. The stricter saturation at six and the sharp volume 150 quantify that loss of information. This is a reusable finite census with a symbolic reduction, not a sample or a renaming of the chain theorem.
